ukberi-tibyan:9-10.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَهَلْ أَتَاكَ حَدِيثُ مُوسَى (٩) إِذْ رَأَى نَارًا فَقَالَ لِأَهْلِهِ امْكُثُوا إِنِّي آنَسْتُ نَارًا لَعَلِّي آتِيكُمْ مِنْهَا بِقَبَسٍ أَوْ أَجِدُ عَلَى النَّارِ هُدًى (١٠)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (إِذْ رَأَى): «إِذْ» is an adverb (ẓarf) for «حَدِيثُ», or a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), i.e. "remember [when]".
(لِأَهْلِهِ): with kasra and with ḍamma on the hāʾ; this has already been mentioned. Whoever reads it with ḍamma makes it follow what comes after it.
And (مِنْهَا): it may be attached to آتيكم, or be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «قَبَسٍ».
The best course with «هُدًى» here is that it be written with alif and not pronounced with imāla (inclination of the vowel), because the alif is a replacement for the tanwīn according to the verified view. Some, however, have pronounced it with imāla, and there are three explanations of this. The first: that he likened the alif of the tanwīn to the final radical (lām) of the word, since in the shortened (maqṣūr) noun the pronunciation of the two is the same. The second: that it is the final radical of the word, and nothing was substituted for the tanwīn in the accusative, as occurs in:
وَآخُذُ مِنْ كُلِّ حَيٍّ عَصُمْ ("and I take from every tribe a pledge [of protection]"). The third: that it follows the view of those who pause in all three states (nominative, accusative and genitive) without any substitution.

ukberi-tibyan:11-12.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (فَلَمَّا أَتَاهَا نُودِيَ يَا مُوسَى (١١) إِنِّي أَنَا رَبُّكَ فَاخْلَعْ نَعْلَيْكَ إِنَّكَ بِالْوَادِي الْمُقَدَّسِ طُوًى (١٢)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (نُودِيَ): the object standing in place of the agent (nāʾib fāʿil, deputy agent) is a concealed pronoun, i.e. "Moses was called". It is also said: it is the maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "the calling was called", and what follows explains it. And «يَا مُوسَى» cannot stand in place of the agent, because it is a clause.
(إِنِّي): it is read with kasra, i.e. "and He said: indeed I…", or because calling is a kind of saying. And with fatḥa, i.e. "he was called with [the words] that I…", just as you say: نَادَيْتُهُ بِاسْمِهِ ("I called him by his name").
And (أَنَا): a mubtadaʾ (subject), or a tawkīd (emphasis), or a separating pronoun (faṣl).
His saying, Exalted is He: (طُوًى): it is read with ḍamma and tanwīn, and it is a proper name for the valley, and it is a badal (substitute) from it. It may also be nominative, i.e. "it is Ṭuwā".
It is also read without tanwīn, on the basis that it is a definite feminine noun, a name for the spot of ground.
It is also said: it is maʿdūl (a form diverted from another), even if the wording of the form it was diverted from is not known; it is as though its origin were «طَاوِي». In that respect it is like جُمَع and كُتَع.
It is also read with kasra, on the basis that it is like عِنَب among nouns, and عِدًا and سِوًى among adjectives.

ukberi-tibyan:13-13.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَأَنَا اخْتَرْتُكَ فَاسْتَمِعْ لِمَا يُوحَى (١٣)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَأَنَا اخْتَرْتُكَ): in the singular form, and this fits better with what precedes it.
It is also read: وَأَنَّا اخْتَرْنَاكَ, in the plural, and the implied form is: "because We have chosen you, so listen"; the lām is then attached to استمع. It may also be conjoined (maʿṭūf) to أَنِّي, i.e. "[he was called] with: Indeed I am your Lord, and with: We have chosen you".

ukberi-tibyan:14-14.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (إِنَّنِي أَنَا اللَّهُ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا أَنَا فَاعْبُدْنِي وَأَقِمِ الصَّلَاةَ لِذِكْرِي (١٤)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (لِذِكْرَى): the lām is attached to أقم, and the implied form is: "at your remembering Me". So the maṣdar (verbal noun) is annexed to its object. It is also said: to its agent, i.e. "for My remembering you", or "[My remembering] it [i.e. the prayer]".
«[Translator's note: the heading is printed «لِذِكْرَى» in the source, while the ayah reads «لِذِكْرِي».]»

ukberi-tibyan:15-15.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (إِنَّ السَّاعَةَ آتِيَةٌ أَكَادُ أُخْفِيهَا لِتُجْزَى كُلُّ نَفْسٍ بِمَا تَسْعَى (١٥)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أُخْفِيهَا): with ḍamma on the hamza, and there are two views on it. One of them: "I conceal it", i.e. from Myself, because He has not disclosed it to any created being. The second: "I reveal it"; it is said that it is one of the words with opposite meanings (aḍdād).
It is also said: the hamza is for privation (salb), i.e. "I remove its hiddenness".
It is also read with fatḥa on the hamza, and its meaning is "I reveal it"; one says: خَفَيْتُ الشَّيْءَ, i.e. "I revealed the thing".
(لِتُجْزَى): the lām is attached to أخفيها. It is also said: to آتية; and for that reason some paused on it with a slight pause, to signal its separation from «أُخْفِيهَا». It is also said: its wording is the wording of kay, while its implied sense is that of an oath, i.e. لَتُجْزَيَنَّ ("it shall surely be recompensed"). And «مَا» is maṣdariyya (forming a verbal noun). It is also said: it is in the sense of الذي, i.e. "[for what] it strives in".

ukberi-tibyan:16-16.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (فَلَا يَصُدَّنَّكَ عَنْهَا مَنْ لَا يُؤْمِنُ بِهَا وَاتَّبَعَ هَوَاهُ فَتَرْدَى (١٦)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فَتَرْدَى): it may be accusative (manṣūb) as the answer to the prohibition, or nominative, i.e. "for then you will perish".

ukberi-tibyan:17-17.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَمَا تِلْكَ بِيَمِينِكَ يَا مُوسَى (١٧)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَمَا تِلْكَ): «مَا» is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and «تِلْكَ» is its khabar (predicate), and it is in the sense of هذه ("this").
And (بِيَمِينِكَ): a ḥāl (circumstantial), governed by the meaning of pointing contained in the demonstrative.
It is also said: it [تلك] is in the sense of الذي; then بيمينك is a ṣifa for it.
«[Translator's note: «صِفَةً لَهَا» here means its complement, i.e. the ṣila (relative clause) of تلك taken as a relative noun.]»

ukberi-tibyan:18-20.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قَالَ هِيَ عَصَايَ أَتَوَكَّأُ عَلَيْهَا وَأَهُشُّ بِهَا عَلَى غَنَمِي وَلِيَ فِيهَا مَآرِبُ أُخْرَى (١٨) قَالَ أَلْقِهَا يَامُوسَى (١٩) فَأَلْقَاهَا فَإِذَا هِيَ حَيَّةٌ تَسْعَى (٢٠)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (عَصَايَ): the proper course is fatḥa on the yāʾ because of the meeting of two quiescent letters.
It is also read with kasra, and this is weak, because it is felt heavy on the yāʾ.
It is also read عَصَىَّ, and its parallel has been mentioned in [Sūrat] al-Baqara.
And (أَتَوَكَّأُ): it and what follows it are resumptive (mustaʾnaf). It is also said: its position is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the yāʾ, or from the staff. It is also said: it is the khabar (predicate) of «هِيَ», and عصاي is the object of an omitted verb. It is also said: it [عصاي] is a khabar, and «أَتَوَكَّأُ» is another khabar.
And (أَهُشُّ): with the dotted shīn, i.e. "I lean on it over the sheep", or "I frighten [them]", and the like.
It is also read with kasra on the hāʾ, i.e. "with it I break down for my sheep what falls on them [of leaves]", from your saying: هَشَشْتُ الْخُبْزَ, when you break bread after it has dried.
It is also read with ḍamma on the hāʾ and an undotted sīn, from your saying: هَسَّ الْغَنَمَ يَهُسُّهَا, when he drives them. It is made transitive with عَلَى because its meaning is "I stand over them with it", or "I frighten [them]".
And (أُخْرَى): according to the feminine of the plural; had He said أُخَر, it would have followed the wording.
(تَسْعَى): it may be a second khabar, and it may be a ḥāl.
And «إِذَا» of surprise (mufājaʾa) is an adverb of place; what governs it is «تَسْعَى» or something omitted. This has already been mentioned.

ukberi-tibyan:21-23.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قَالَ خُذْهَا وَلَا تَخَفْ سَنُعِيدُهَا سِيرَتَهَا الْأُولَى (٢١) وَاضْمُمْ يَدَكَ إِلَى جَنَاحِكَ تَخْرُجْ بَيْضَاءَ مِنْ غَيْرِ سُوءٍ آيَةً أُخْرَى (٢٢) لِنُرِيَكَ مِنْ آيَاتِنَا الْكُبْرَى (٢٣)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (سِيرَتَهَا الْأُولَى): it is a badal (substitute) from the object pronoun, a badal of inclusion (badal al-ishtimāl), because the meaning of سيرتها is "its state" or "its manner".
It may also be an adverb (ẓarf), i.e. "in its [former] manner".
It is also said: the implied form is: "to its [former] state".
And (بَيْضَاءَ): a ḥāl (circumstantial).
And (مِنْ غَيْرِ سُوءٍ): it may be attached to (تَخْرُجُ), or be an adjective (ṣifa) of (بَيْضَاءَ), or a ḥāl from the pronoun in (بَيْضَاءَ). And (آيَةً): a ḥāl that is a badal from the first [ḥāl], or a ḥāl from the pronoun in بيضاء, i.e. "it turns white as a sign", or a ḥāl from the pronoun in the prepositional phrase. It is also said: it is accusative by an omitted verb, i.e. "and We made it a sign", or "We gave you a sign".
And (لِنُرِيَكَ): attached to this omitted [verb]. It may also be attached to what آية indicates, i.e. "We gave proof by it in order to show you". It is not attached to آية itself, because it has been qualified by an adjective.
And (الْكُبْرَى): an adjective of آيات, and its rule is the rule of «مَآرِبُ» [i.e. «أُخْرَى» in ayah 18]. Had He said الكُبَر, it would have been permissible. It may also be that الكبرى is accusative by «نُرِيَكَ», and «مِنْ آيَاتِنَا» is a ḥāl from it, i.e. "in order to show you the greatest sign from among Our signs".

ukberi-tibyan:25-27.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قَالَ رَبِّ اشْرَحْ لِي صَدْرِي (٢٥) وَيَسِّرْ لِي أَمْرِي (٢٦) وَاحْلُلْ عُقْدَةً مِنْ لِسَانِي (٢٧)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَيَسِّرْ لِي): one says: يَسَّرْتُ لَهُ كَذَا ("I made such-and-such easy for him"), and this ayah is of that kind; and يَسَّرْتُهُ لِكَذَا ("I made him ready for such-and-such"), and of that kind is
His saying, Exalted is He: (فَسَنُيَسِّرُهُ لِلْيُسْرَى).
And (مِنْ لِسَانِي): it may be attached to احلل, or be an adjective of عقدة.

ukberi-tibyan:29-32.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَاجْعَلْ لِي وَزِيرًا مِنْ أَهْلِي (٢٩) هَارُونَ أَخِي (٣٠) اشْدُدْ بِهِ أَزْرِي (٣١) وَأَشْرِكْهُ فِي أَمْرِي (٣٢)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَزِيرًا): the wāw is original, because it is from الوِزْر ("burden") and المُوَازَرَة ("helping to bear a burden").
It is also said: it is a replacement for a hamza, because the minister strengthens the back (أَزْر) of the one he assists; but this is rare. The pattern faʿīl here is in the sense of the active participle, like العَشِير ("companion") and الخَلِيط ("associate").
Concerning the two objects of «اجْعَلْ» there are three views. One of them: that they are «وَزِيرًا» and «هَارُونَ», but the second object has been placed first; on this view «لِي» may be attached to اجعل, or be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from وزير. The second: that «وَزِيرًا» is the first object and «لِي» the second; and «هَارُونَ» is a badal (substitute) or an ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition), and
«أَخِي» likewise. The third: that the second object is «مِنْ أَهْلِي», and «لِي» is for clarification (tabyīn), like His saying: (وَلَمْ يَكُنْ لَهُ كُفُوًا أَحَدٌ); and «هَارُونَ أَخِي» is as stated before. (هَارُونَ) may also be accusative by an omitted verb, i.e. "join Hārūn to me". His saying, Exalted is He: (اشْدُدْ): it is read with a disjunctive hamza (hamzat al-qaṭʿ). (وَأَشْرِكْهُ): with ḍamma on the hamza, and jussive as the answer to the supplication, the verb being attributed to Moses; and the two are [also] read in the form of the imperative.
«[Translator's note: the variant meant is أَشْدُدْ… وَأُشْرِكْهُ, first-person jussives ("I shall strengthen… and I shall make him share"); the text as printed compresses this.]»

ukberi-tibyan:33-34.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (كَيْ نُسَبِّحَكَ كَثِيرًا (٣٣) وَنَذْكُرَكَ كَثِيرًا (٣٤)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (كَثِيرًا): i.e. "much glorification", or "for a long time".

ukberi-tibyan:36-36.t: Allah the Exalted says: (قَدْ أُوتِيتَ سُؤْلَكَ يَا مُوسَى (٣٦)). السُّؤَال and السُّؤْل are in the sense of the passive participle ("what is asked for"), like الأُكْل in the sense of المأكول ("what is eaten").

ukberi-tibyan:38-40.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (إِذْ أَوْحَيْنَا إِلَى أُمِّكَ مَا يُوحَى (٣٨) أَنِ اقْذِفِيهِ فِي التَّابُوتِ فَاقْذِفِيهِ فِي الْيَمِّ فَلْيُلْقِهِ الْيَمُّ بِالسَّاحِلِ يَأْخُذْهُ عَدُوٌّ لِي وَعَدُوٌّ لَهُ وَأَلْقَيْتُ عَلَيْكَ مَحَبَّةً مِنِّي وَلِتُصْنَعَ عَلَى عَيْنِي (٣٩) إِذْ تَمْشِي أُخْتُكَ فَتَقُولُ هَلْ أَدُلُّكُمْ عَلَى مَنْ يَكْفُلُهُ فَرَجَعْنَاكَ إِلَى أُمِّكَ كَيْ تَقَرَّ عَيْنُهَا وَلَا تَحْزَنَ وَقَتَلْتَ نَفْسًا فَنَجَّيْنَاكَ مِنَ الْغَمِّ وَفَتَنَّاكَ فُتُونًا فَلَبِثْتَ سِنِينَ فِي أَهْلِ مَدْيَنَ ثُمَّ جِئْتَ عَلَى قَدَرٍ يَامُوسَى (٤٠)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (إِذْ أَوْحَيْنَا): it is an adverb (ẓarf) for مَنَنَّا ("We conferred a favour", ayah 37).
(أَنِ اقْذِفِيهِ): (أَنْ) may be maṣdariyya (forming a verbal noun), as a badal (substitute) from (مَا يُوحَى), or on the implied form: "it is: that you cast him"; and it may be in the sense of أَيْ ("namely", explicative). (فَلْيُلْقِهِ): a command to the absent [third person]. And (مِنِّي): attached to ألقيت; and it may be a naʿt (adjective) of «مَحَبَّةً». And (لِتُصْنَعَ): i.e. "so that you be loved and so that you be reared".
It is also read in the form of the command [وَلْتُصْنَعْ], i.e. "let another rear you by My command".
It is also read with kasra on the lām and fatḥa on the tāʾ and the ʿayn [وَلِتَصْنَعَ], i.e. "so that you do what I command you, within My sight".
(إِذْ تَمْشِي): it may be attached to either of the two verbs, or be a badal from the first «إِذْ», because his sister's walking was a favour to him; or the implied form may be: "remember when [your sister] walked".
And (فُتُونًا): a maṣdar (verbal noun) like القُعُود. It may also be a plural, its implied form being: "with many trials", i.e. with matters by which you were tested. And (عَلَى قَدَرٍ): a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "in accordance with what was decreed for you".

ukberi-tibyan:45-45.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قَالَا رَبَّنَا إِنَّنَا نَخَافُ أَنْ يَفْرُطَ عَلَيْنَا أَوْ أَنْ يَطْغَى (٤٥)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَنْ يَفْرُطَ): the majority read it with fatḥa on the yāʾ and ḍamma on the rāʾ. The implied form may be: "that a word should hastily come forth from him against us"; the word (القول) is left concealed because the situation indicates it, just as you say:
فَرَطَ مِنِّي قَوْلٌ ("a word escaped from me hastily"). Or the fāʿil (agent) may be a pronoun referring to Pharaoh, as it is in «يَطْغَى».

ukberi-tibyan:49-50.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قَالَ فَمَنْ رَبُّكُمَا يَا مُوسَى (٤٩) قَالَ رَبُّنَا الَّذِي أَعْطَى كُلَّ شَيْءٍ خَلْقَهُ ثُمَّ هَدَى (٥٠)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فَمَنْ رَبُّكُمَا يَامُوسَى): i.e. "and Hārūn"; it was omitted because it is known.
It may also be that he sought the answer from Moses alone, since he was the principal; and for that reason He said: «قَالَ رَبُّنَا الَّذِي». And (خَلْقَهُ): the first object, and (كُلَّ شَيْءٍ): the second, i.e. "He gave His creation everything".
It is also said: it is in its [natural] order, and the meaning is: "He gave every created thing its form (خلقه)", i.e. He is the one who originated it. It is also read «خَلَقَهُ» as a verb ("He created it"), and the second object is omitted because it is known.

ukberi-tibyan:52-52.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قَالَ عِلْمُهَا عِنْدَ رَبِّي فِي كِتَابٍ لَا يَضِلُّ رَبِّي وَلَا يَنْسَى (٥٢)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (عِلْمُهَا): a mubtadaʾ (subject), and concerning the khabar (predicate) there are several views. One of them: it is «عِنْدَ رَبِّي», and on this view «فِي كِتَابٍ» is governed by the khabar, or is a second khabar, or a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in «عِنْدَ». The second: that the khabar is «فِي كِتَابٍ», and «عِنْدَ» is a ḥāl, governed by the adverbial phrase after it, according to the view of al-Akhfash. It is also said: it is a ḥāl from the muḍāf ilayhi in «عِلْمُهَا». It is also said: it is an adverb for the second adverbial phrase. It is also said: it is an adverb for العلم ("the knowledge"). The third: that the two adverbial phrases together form one khabar, like هَذَا حُلْوٌ حَامِضٌ ("this is sweet-sour"). It is not permissible for «فِي كِتَابٍ» to be attached to عِلْمُهَا with «عِنْدَ» as the khabar, because a maṣdar (verbal noun) does not govern what comes after its khabar.
(لَا يَضِلُّ): in the position of the genitive as an adjective of كتاب. Concerning the implied sense there are two views. One of them: "my Lord does not go astray from preserving it". The second: "the book does not escape my Lord", i.e. "from Him"; so (رَبِّي) is an object.
It is also read with ḍamma on the yāʾ, i.e. "no one causes my Lord to go astray from His knowledge".
It may also be that ربي is the agent, i.e. "He does not find the book lost", i.e. gone astray, as in His saying, Exalted is He: (ضَلَّ مَنْ تَدْعُونَ).
And the object of «يَنْسَى» is omitted, i.e. "and He does not forget it".
It is also read with ḍamma on the yāʾ, i.e. "no one causes my Lord to forget", or "the book is not forgotten".
«[Translator's note: in the first reading the text writes «لَا يُضِلُّ» with ḍamma, though the sense given ("does not go astray") corresponds to يَضِلُّ; the bracketed «[لَا]» in the next sentence is the editor's addition.]»

ukberi-tibyan:53-54.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (الَّذِي جَعَلَ لَكُمُ الْأَرْضَ مَهْدًا وَسَلَكَ لَكُمْ فِيهَا سُبُلًا وَأَنْزَلَ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ مَاءً فَأَخْرَجْنَا بِهِ أَزْوَاجًا مِنْ نَبَاتٍ شَتَّى (٥٣) كُلُوا وَارْعَوْا أَنْعَامَكُمْ إِنَّ فِي ذَلِكَ لَآيَاتٍ لِأُولِي النُّهَى (٥٤)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مَهْدًا): it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) used as an adjective; the implied form may also be: "possessing a cradle-like spread".
It is also read (مِهَادًا), like فِرَاش ("bed"); and it may be the plural of مَهْد. (شَتَّى): plural of شَتِيت ("scattered, diverse"), like مَرِيض and مَرْضَى; it is an adjective of أزواج, or of نبات.
And (النَّهْيُ): plural of نُهْيَة ("intellect"). It is also said: it is singular.
«[Translator's note: the text has «لَبِنَاتٍ», evidently a misprint for «لِنَبَاتٍ» ("of نبات"); and the heading «النَّهْيُ» stands for the Quranic «النُّهَى».]»

ukberi-tibyan:58-58.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (فَلَنَأْتِيَنَّكَ بِسِحْرٍ مِثْلِهِ فَاجْعَلْ بَيْنَنَا وَبَيْنَكَ مَوْعِدًا لَا نُخْلِفُهُ نَحْنُ وَلَا أَنْتَ مَكَانًا سُوًى (٥٨)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (بِسِحْرٍ مِثْلِهِ): it may be attached to لنأتينك, or be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agents.
(فَاجْعَلْ بَيْنَنَا وَبَيْنَكَ مَوْعِدًا): here it is a maṣdar (verbal noun), because of His saying, Exalted is He: (لَا نُخْلِفُهُ نَحْنُ وَلَا أَنْتَ مَكَانًا), i.e. "in a place". And (سِوًى) with kasra is an anomalous adjective; like it is قَوْمٌ عِدًا ("a hostile people"). It is also read with ḍamma, which is more common among adjectives, and its meaning is "midway". «مَكَانًا» may also be
the second object of اجعل, and on this view موعدًا is also a place. It is not accusative by موعد, because it is a maṣdar that has been qualified by an adjective. It has also been read: سِوَى without tanwīn, treating continuous speech as if it were a pause.

ukberi-tibyan:59-59.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قَالَ مَوْعِدُكُمْ يَوْمُ الزِّينَةِ وَأَنْ يُحْشَرَ النَّاسُ ضُحًى (٥٩)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (قَالَ مَوْعِدُكُمْ): it is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and «يَوْمُ الزِّينَةِ» in the nominative is the khabar (predicate). If you make موعد a [noun of] time, the second is the same as the first; and if you make موعد a maṣdar (verbal noun), the implied form is: "the time of your appointment is the day of adornment". «يَوْمَ» is also read in the accusative, on the basis that «مَوْعِد» is a maṣdar and the adverb is the khabar
about it, i.e. "your appointment takes place on the day of adornment"; and it is a maṣdar in the sense of the passive participle. (وَأَنْ يُحْشَرَ النَّاسُ): conjoined (maʿṭūf), and the implied form is: "and the day when the people are gathered"; so it is in the position of the genitive. It may also be in the position of the nominative, i.e. "your appointment is that the people be gathered". It is also read «تَحْشُرَ» with the agent named, i.e. Pharaoh [you, Pharaoh, gather], with النَّاسَ accusative.

ukberi-tibyan:61-61.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قَالَ لَهُمْ مُوسَى وَيْلَكُمْ لَا تَفْتَرُوا عَلَى اللَّهِ كَذِبًا فَيُسْحِتَكُمْ بِعَذَابٍ وَقَدْ خَابَ مَنِ افْتَرَى (٦١)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فَيُسْحِتَكُمْ): it is read with fatḥa on the yāʾ and with ḍamma, the past tense being سَحَتَ and أَسْحَتَ, two dialectal forms; and it is accusative as the answer to the prohibition.

ukberi-tibyan:63-63.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قَالُوا إِنْ هَذَانِ لَسَاحِرَانِ يُرِيدَانِ أَنْ يُخْرِجَاكُمْ مِنْ أَرْضِكُمْ بِسِحْرِهِمَا وَيَذْهَبَا بِطَرِيقَتِكُمُ الْمُثْلَى (٦٣)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (إِنَّ هَذَيْنِ): it is read with a doubled (shadda) إنّ and with yāʾ in هذين, which is the sign of the accusative.
(إِنَّ) is also read with the shadda and هذان with alif, and there are several explanations of this. One of them: that it is in the sense of نَعَمْ ("yes"), and what follows it is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). The second: that إنّ has an omitted pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn) in it, and what follows it is likewise a mubtadaʾ and khabar. Both explanations are weak because of the lām in the khabar; something like that occurs only under the necessity of poetry.
Al-Zajjāj said: the implied form is: لَهُمَا سَاحِرَانِ ("they two are surely two sorcerers"), and the mubtadaʾ was omitted.
The third: that the alif here is the sign of the dual in every state. This is the dialect of Banū al-Ḥārith; it is also said: of Kināna.
(إِنْ) is also read light (without shadda). It is said that it is lightened from the heavy [إنّ], and this too is weak.
It is also said: it is in the sense of «مَا» (negation) and the lām is in the sense of «إِلَّا» ("except"); its parallels have preceded.
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَيَذْهَبَا بِطَرِيقَتِكُمُ): i.e. "and do away with your way"; the bāʾ makes the verb transitive, just as the hamza makes it transitive.

ukberi-tibyan:64-64.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (فَأَجْمِعُوا كَيْدَكُمْ ثُمَّ ائْتُوا صَفًّا وَقَدْ أَفْلَحَ الْيَوْمَ مَنِ اسْتَعْلَى (٦٤)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فَأَجْمِعُوا): it is read with a connecting hamza (hamzat al-waṣl) and fatḥa on the mīm [فَاجْمَعُوا], and it is from الجَمْع ("gathering"), which is the opposite of scattering; this is indicated by His saying, Exalted is He: (فَجَمَعَ كَيْدَهُ). And الكيد means that by which one plots.
It is also read with a disjunctive hamza and kasra on the mīm, and this is a dialectal form of جَمَعَ; al-Akhfash said so.
It is also said: the implied form is: "[resolve] upon your plot".
And (صَفًّا): a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "lined up in ranks". It is also said: a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), i.e. "make for the ranks of your enemies".

ukberi-tibyan:65-65.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قَالُوا يَا مُوسَى إِمَّا أَنْ تُلْقِيَ وَإِمَّا أَنْ نَكُونَ أَوَّلَ مَنْ أَلْقَى (٦٥)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (إِمَّا أَنْ تُلْقِيَ): this has been mentioned in [Sūrat] al-Aʿrāf.

ukberi-tibyan:66-66.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قَالَ بَلْ أَلْقُوا فَإِذَا حِبَالُهُمْ وَعِصِيُّهُمْ يُخَيَّلُ إِلَيْهِ مِنْ سِحْرِهِمْ أَنَّهَا تَسْعَى (٦٦)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فَإِذَا): it is [the إذا] of surprise (mufājaʾa).
And (حِبَالُهُمْ): a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the khabar (predicate) is إذا; on this view «يُخَيَّلُ» is a ḥāl (circumstantial); or, if you wish, «يُخَيَّلُ» is the khabar.
And (يُخَيَّلُ) with yāʾ, on the basis that it is attributed to the moving, i.e. "their moving was made to seem to them"; it may also be attributed to the pronoun of the ropes, and it is put in the masculine because the femininity is not real; or it is on the implied form: "what was thrown was made to seem". And (أَنَّهَا تَسْعَى): a badal (substitute) from it, a badal of inclusion (badal al-ishtimāl). It may also be in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl, i.e. "the ropes were made to seem possessed of movement". Whoever reads it with tāʾ [تُخَيَّلُ] has the pronoun of the ropes in it, and «أَنَّهَا تَسْعَى» is a badal from it. It is also said: it is in the position of the accusative, i.e. "it was made to seem to them that they were possessed of movement". It is also read with fatḥa on the tāʾ and kasra on the yāʾ [تَخَيَّلُ], i.e. "the ropes make their movement seem [real] to them".
«[Translator's note: the text says «إِلَيْهِمْ» ("to them") in the glosses, while the ayah has «إِلَيْهِ» ("to him"). Also, the last reading is described as fatḥa on the tāʾ and kasra on the yāʾ, while the gloss «تُخَيِّلُ» is vowelled with ḍamma on the tāʾ.]»

ukberi-tibyan:69-69.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَأَلْقِ مَا فِي يَمِينِكَ تَلْقَفْ مَا صَنَعُوا إِنَّمَا صَنَعُوا كَيْدُ سَاحِرٍ وَلَا يُفْلِحُ السَّاحِرُ حَيْثُ أَتَى (٦٩)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (تَلْقَفْ): it is read in the jussive as the answer [to the imperative]; the fāʿil (agent) is a pronoun referring to «مَا», and it is feminine because He meant the staff.
It may also be a pronoun referring to Moses, upon him be peace; this is attributed to him because it happens through his agency.
It is also read with ḍamma on the fāʾ [تَلْقَفُ], on the basis that it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the staff or from Moses, and it is an anticipated ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara). Doubling the qāf and leaving it light are two readings with one meaning.
As for doubling the qāf, it is on the implied form تَتَلَقَّفْ; the like of it has been mentioned in several places.
(إِنَّ مَا صَنَعُوا): whoever reads «كَيْدُ» in the nominative, there are two views on «مَا». One of them: it is in the sense of الذي, and the returning pronoun is omitted. The second: it is maṣdariyya (forming a verbal noun).
It is also read in the accusative [كَيْدَ], on the basis that «مَا» is the restraining mā (kāffa); and the annexation of «كَيْد» to «سَاحِر» is the annexation of the maṣdar (verbal noun) to its agent.
It was also read كَيْدُ سِحْرٍ, and this is the annexation of the genus to the species.
«[Translator's note: the text writes «كَيَدُ» with fatḥa on the yāʾ, and «الْمُصَدِّرِ» for «الْمَصْدَرِ»; both appear to be misprints.]»

ukberi-tibyan:71-71.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قَالَ آمَنْتُمْ لَهُ قَبْلَ أَنْ آذَنَ لَكُمْ إِنَّهُ لَكَبِيرُكُمُ الَّذِي عَلَّمَكُمُ السِّحْرَ فَلَأُقَطِّعَنَّ أَيْدِيَكُمْ وَأَرْجُلَكُمْ مِنْ خِلَافٍ وَلَأُصَلِّبَنَّكُمْ فِي جُذُوعِ النَّخْلِ وَلَتَعْلَمُنَّ أَيُّنَا أَشَدُّ عَذَابًا وَأَبْقَى (٧١)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فِي جُذُوعِ النَّخْلِ): «فِي» here has its basic meaning, because the trunk is a place for the one crucified and contains him. It is also said: it is in the sense of عَلَى ("on").

ukberi-tibyan:72-72.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قَالُوا لَنْ نُؤْثِرَكَ عَلَى مَا جَاءَنَا مِنَ الْبَيِّنَاتِ وَالَّذِي فَطَرَنَا فَاقْضِ مَا أَنْتَ قَاضٍ إِنَّمَا تَقْضِي هَذِهِ الْحَيَاةَ الدُّنْيَا (٧٢))
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَالَّذِي فَطَرَنَا): in the position of the genitive, i.e. "and over the One who [created us]". It is also said: it is an oath.
(مَا أَنْتَ قَاضٍ): concerning «مَا» there are two views. One of them: it is in the sense of الذي, i.e. "do that which you are resolved upon". The second: it is temporal, i.e. "carry out your affair for as long as you are carrying it out".
(هَذِهِ الْحَيَاةَ الدُّنْيَا): it is accusative by تقضي, and «مَا» is the restraining mā (kāffa), i.e. "you decide the affairs of this worldly life".
It may also be an adverb (ẓarf), with the object omitted. If it has been read in the nominative, then it is the khabar (predicate) of إنّ.

ukberi-tibyan:73-73.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (إِنَّا آمَنَّا بِرَبِّنَا لِيَغْفِرَ لَنَا خَطَايَانَا وَمَا أَكْرَهْتَنَا عَلَيْهِ مِنَ السِّحْرِ وَاللَّهُ خَيْرٌ وَأَبْقَى (٧٣)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَمَا أَكْرَهْتَنَا): concerning «مَا» there are two views. One of them: it is in the sense of الذي, conjoined to الخطايا. It is also said: [on this view] it is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), with the khabar (predicate) omitted, i.e. "and what you compelled us to is dropped" or "remitted".
And (مِنَ السِّحْرِ): a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «مَا» or from the hāʾ.
The second: it is negating, and there is a fronting in the sentence; its implied form is: "that He may forgive us our sins of sorcery, and you did not compel us to it".

ukberi-tibyan:74-74.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (إِنَّهُ مَنْ يَأْتِ رَبَّهُ مُجْرِمًا فَإِنَّ لَهُ جَهَنَّمَ لَا يَمُوتُ فِيهَا وَلَا يَحْيَا (٧٤)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (إِنَّهُ مَنْ يَأْتِ): the pronoun is the pronoun of the matter and the story (ḍamīr al-shaʾn wa-l-qiṣṣa).

ukberi-tibyan:76-76.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (جَنَّاتُ عَدْنٍ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهَارُ خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا وَذَلِكَ جَزَاءُ مَنْ تَزَكَّى (٧٦)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (جَنَّاتُ عَدْنٍ): it is a badal (substitute) from الدرجات (ayah 75). It is not permissible for the implied form to be "they are gardens", because «خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا» is a ḥāl (circumstantial), and on that implied form there would be nothing in the sentence to govern the ḥāl; whereas on the first view, what governs the ḥāl is the [implied] notion of being settled (al-istiqrār), or the meaning of pointing [in the demonstrative].

ukberi-tibyan:77-77.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَلَقَدْ أَوْحَيْنَا إِلَى مُوسَى أَنْ أَسْرِ بِعِبَادِي فَاضْرِبْ لَهُمْ طَرِيقًا فِي الْبَحْرِ يَبَسًا لَا تَخَافُ دَرَكًا وَلَا تَخْشَى (٧٧)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فَاضْرِبْ لَهُمْ طَرِيقًا): the implied form is: "the place of a road"; so it is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) on the overt reading. Its parallel is His saying, Exalted is He: (أَنِ اضْرِبْ بِعَصَاكَ الْبَحْرَ), and it is like ضَرَبْتُ زَيْدًا ("I struck Zayd"). It is also said: ضرب here is in the sense of "made" and "laid out", like their saying: ضَرَبْتُ لَهُ بِسَهْمٍ ("I assigned him a share").
And (يَبَسًا) with fatḥa on the bāʾ: a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "possessing dryness"; or He described it by the maṣdar for intensification. As for اليُبْس with sukūn on the bāʾ, it is an adjective in the sense of اليابس ("dry").
(لَا تَخَافُ): concerning the nominative there are three views. One of them: it is resumptive (mustaʾnaf). The second: it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in «اضْرِبْ». The third: it is an adjective of the road, and the returning pronoun is omitted, i.e. "and he does not fear in it".
It is also read in the jussive [لَا تَخَفْ], as a prohibition, or as the answer to the command.
As for «لَا تَخْشَى», on the first reading it is nominative like what it is conjoined to. The implied form may also be: "while you do not fear".
On the jussive reading it is a ḥāl, i.e. "while you do not fear". The implied form may also be: "so strike for them [a road], not fearing".
It is also said: the alif is [treated as] in the implied jussive, being likened to the sound (non-weak) letters.
It is also said: it arose through lengthening of the fatḥa, so that the ends of the ayahs agree.

ukberi-tibyan:78-78.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (فَأَتْبَعَهُمْ فِرْعَوْنُ بِجُنُودِهِ فَغَشِيَهُمْ مِنَ الْيَمِّ مَا غَشِيَهُمْ (٧٨)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (بِجُنُودِهِ): it is in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial), and the second object is omitted, i.e. "Pharaoh made his punishment follow them, with his troops along with him". It is also said: أَتْبَعَ is in the sense of اتَّبَعَ ("followed"); so the bāʾ makes the verb transitive.

ukberi-tibyan:80-81.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (يَا بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ قَدْ أَنْجَيْنَاكُمْ مِنْ عَدُوِّكُمْ وَوَاعَدْنَاكُمْ جَانِبَ الطُّورِ الْأَيْمَنَ وَنَزَّلْنَا عَلَيْكُمُ الْمَنَّ وَالسَّلْوَى (٨٠) كُلُوا مِنْ طَيِّبَاتِ مَا رَزَقْنَاكُمْ وَلَا تَطْغَوْا فِيهِ فَيَحِلَّ عَلَيْكُمْ غَضَبِي وَمَنْ يَحْلِلْ عَلَيْهِ غَضَبِي فَقَدْ هَوَى (٨١))
His saying, Exalted is He: (جَانِبَ الطُّورِ): it is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), i.e. "[We appointed with you] the coming to the side of the Mount"; it cannot be an adverb (ẓarf), because it is a specific [place].
(فَيَحِلَّ): it is the answer to the prohibition. It is also said: it is conjoined, so it too is a prohibition, as in their saying: لَا تَمْدُدْهَا فَتَشُقَّهَا ("do not stretch it and so tear it").
And (مَنْ يَحْلِلْ): with ḍamma on the lām [يَحْلُلْ], i.e. "descends", as in His saying, Exalted is He: (أَوْ تَحُلُّ قَرِيبًا مِنْ دَارِهِمْ).
And with kasra, in the sense of "becomes due", as in His saying: (وَيَحِلُّ عَلَيْهِ عَذَابٌ مُقِيمٌ).

ukberi-tibyan:83-83.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَمَا أَعْجَلَكَ عَنْ قَوْمِكَ يَا مُوسَى (٨٣)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَمَا أَعْجَلَكَ): «مَا» is interrogative, a mubtadaʾ (subject), and «أَعْجَلَكَ» is the khabar (predicate).

ukberi-tibyan:84-84.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قَالَ هُمْ أُولَاءِ عَلَى أَثَرِي وَعَجِلْتُ إِلَيْكَ رَبِّ لِتَرْضَى (٨٤)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (هُمْ): a mubtadaʾ (subject), and (أُولَاءِ) is in the sense of الذي; (عَلَى أَثَرِي) is its ṣila (relative clause). This has been mentioned exhaustively at His saying: (ثُمَّ أَنْتُمْ هَؤُلَاءِ تَقْتُلُونَ).

ukberi-tibyan:86-86.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (فَرَجَعَ مُوسَى إِلَى قَوْمِهِ غَضْبَانَ أَسِفًا قَالَ يَا قَوْمِ أَلَمْ يَعِدْكُمْ رَبُّكُمْ وَعْدًا حَسَنًا أَفَطَالَ عَلَيْكُمُ الْعَهْدُ أَمْ أَرَدْتُمْ أَنْ يَحِلَّ عَلَيْكُمْ غَضَبٌ مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ فَأَخْلَفْتُمْ مَوْعِدِي (٨٦)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَعْدًا حَسَنًا): it may be an emphasising maṣdar (mafʿūl muṭlaq, absolute object), or a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) in the sense of "the thing promised".

ukberi-tibyan:87-88.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قَالُوا مَا أَخْلَفْنَا مَوْعِدَكَ بِمَلْكِنَا وَلَكِنَّا حُمِّلْنَا أَوْزَارًا مِنْ زِينَةِ الْقَوْمِ فَقَذَفْنَاهَا فَكَذَلِكَ أَلْقَى السَّامِرِيُّ (٨٧) فَأَخْرَجَ لَهُمْ عِجْلًا جَسَدًا لَهُ خُوَارٌ فَقَالُوا هَذَا إِلَهُكُمْ وَإِلَهُ مُوسَى فَنَسِيَ (٨٨)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (بِمَلْكِنَا): it is read with kasra, fatḥa and ḍamma on the mīm, and there are two views on it. One of them: that they are dialectal variants, and all of them are a maṣdar (verbal noun) meaning "power". The second: that the ḍamma form is the maṣdar of «مَلِك» ("king"); one says: مَلِكٌ بَيِّنُ الْمُلْكِ ("a king of evident kingship"). The fatḥa form is in the sense of "what is owned"; [i.e. by setting right what he owns. The kasra form is the maṣdar of مالك ("owner"), and it may also be in the sense of what is owned]. When it is taken as a maṣdar, it is annexed to its agent and the object is omitted, i.e. "by our controlling our affair", or "the right course", or "the error".
(حُمِّلْنَا): [read] light [حَمَلْنَا]. It is also read with the shadda, in the passive (with the agent unnamed), i.e. "our people made us carry".
(فَكَذَلِكَ): an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. "a throwing like that".
The fāʿil (agent) of «نَسِيَ» is Moses, upon him be peace, and it is a report of his people's words. It is also said: the agent is a pronoun referring to al-Sāmirī.
«[Translator's note: the text has «بَيَّنُ», evidently for «بَيِّنُ». The passage in square brackets is so in the source.]»

ukberi-tibyan:89-89.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (أَفَلَا يَرَوْنَ أَلَّا يَرْجِعُ إِلَيْهِمْ قَوْلًا وَلَا يَمْلِكُ لَهُمْ ضَرًّا وَلَا نَفْعًا (٨٩)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَنْ لَا يَرْجِعُ): أنْ is lightened from the heavy [أنّ], and «لَا» is like a compensation for its omitted noun. «يَرْجِعَ» has also been read in the accusative, on the basis that «أَنْ» is the one that makes the verb accusative; this is weak, because «يَرْجِعُ» [i.e. the governing verb] is among the verbs of certainty. We have mentioned this at His saying: (وَحَسِبُوا أَنْ لَا تَكُونَ).
«[Translator's note: the verb of certainty is evidently «يَرَوْنَ», not «يَرْجِعُ», as the text has it.]»

ukberi-tibyan:92-94.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قَالَ يَا هَارُونُ مَا مَنَعَكَ إِذْ رَأَيْتَهُمْ ضَلُّوا (٩٢) أَلَّا تَتَّبِعَنِي أَفَعَصَيْتَ أَمْرِي (٩٣) قَالَ يَاابْنَ أُمَّ لَا تَأْخُذْ بِلِحْيَتِي وَلَا بِرَأْسِي إِنِّي خَشِيتُ أَنْ تَقُولَ فَرَّقْتَ بَيْنَ بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ وَلَمْ تَرْقُبْ قَوْلِي (٩٤)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَنْ لَا تَتَّبِعَنِ): لا is redundant (zāʾida), like His saying: (مَا مَنَعَكَ أَنْ لَا تَسْجُدَ); this has been mentioned.
And (يَا ابْنَ أُمَّ): this has been mentioned in [Sūrat] al-Aʿrāf.
(لَا تَأْخُذْ بِلِحْيَتِي): the meaning is "do not seize me by my beard"; that is why the bāʾ comes in. Fatḥa on the lām [بِلَحْيَتِي] is a dialectal form, and it has been read with both.

ukberi-tibyan:96-96.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قَالَ بَصُرْتُ بِمَا لَمْ يَبْصُرُوا بِهِ فَقَبَضْتُ قَبْضَةً مِنْ أَثَرِ الرَّسُولِ فَنَبَذْتُهَا وَكَذَلِكَ سَوَّلَتْ لِي نَفْسِي (٩٦)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (بَصُرْتُ بِمَا لَمْ يَبْصُرُوا): it is made transitive by a preposition; if you bring in the hamza [أَبْصَرَ], it becomes transitive by itself, like فَرِحَ ("he rejoiced") and أَفْرَحْتَهُ ("you made him rejoice"). يبصروا with yāʾ is in the third person, meaning the people of Moses; and with tāʾ it is in the second person, the one addressed being Moses alone, but the pronoun is plural because his people are subordinate to him.
It was also read بَصِرْتُ with kasra on the ṣād, and تَبْصَرُوا with fatḥa on it; this is a dialectal form.
(قَبَضْتُ) with ḍād means [taking] with the full palm, and with ṣād [قَبَصْتُ] with the fingertips; it has been read so.
And (قَبْضَةً): a maṣdar (verbal noun), with ḍād and with ṣād. It may also be in the sense of "the thing taken", so it is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
It is also read قُبْضَةً with ḍamma on the qāf, in the sense of "the thing taken".

ukberi-tibyan:97-97.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قَالَ فَاذْهَبْ فَإِنَّ لَكَ فِي الْحَيَاةِ أَنْ تَقُولَ لَا مِسَاسَ وَإِنَّ لَكَ مَوْعِدًا لَنْ تُخْلَفَهُ وَانْظُرْ إِلَى إِلَهِكَ الَّذِي ظَلْتَ عَلَيْهِ عَاكِفًا لَنُحَرِّقَنَّهُ ثُمَّ لَنَنْسِفَنَّهُ فِي الْيَمِّ نَسْفًا (٩٧)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (لَا مِسَاسَ): it is read with kasra on the mīm and fatḥa on the sīn, and it is the maṣdar (verbal noun) of مَاسَّهُ ("he touched him"), i.e. "I shall not touch you and you shall not touch me".
It is also read with fatḥa on the mīm and kasra on the sīn [مَسَاسِ], and it is a verbal noun of command (ism fiʿl), i.e. "do not touch me". It is also said: it is a noun standing for a statement, i.e. "there shall be no touching between us".
(لَنْ تُخْلَفَهُ): with ḍamma on the tāʾ and kasra on the lām [تُخْلِفَهُ], i.e. "you will not find it broken", like أَحْمَدْتُهُ ("I found him praiseworthy") and أَحْبَبْتُهُ.
It is also said: the meaning is "it will reach you", as though he will fulfil it.
It is also read with ḍamma on the tāʾ and fatḥa on the lām, in the passive (with the agent unnamed).
It is also read with nūn and kasra on the lām [نُخْلِفَهُ], i.e. لَنْ نُخْلِفَكَهُ ("We shall not fail you in it"); the first object was omitted.
His saying, Exalted is He: (ظَلْتَ): it is read with fatḥa and with kasra on the ẓāʾ, and they are two dialectal forms. The origin is ظَلِلْتَ with kasra on the first lām; it was omitted and its kasra was transferred to the ẓāʾ. Whoever reads with fatḥa does not transfer it.
(لَنُحَرِّقَنَّهُ): with the shadda, from burning with fire. It is also said: it is from حَرَقَ نَابُ الْبَعِيرِ, when [the camel grinds its teeth] one upon another; the meaning is "We shall surely file it down", and it is doubled for intensity.
It is also read with ḍamma on the rāʾ and light [لَنَحْرُقَنَّهُ], and this is a dialectal form of the grinding of the camel's tooth.
(لَنَنْسِفَنَّهُ): with kasra and with ḍamma on the sīn; they are two dialectal forms, and both have been read.

ukberi-tibyan:98-99.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (إِنَّمَا إِلَهُكُمُ اللَّهُ الَّذِي لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ وَسِعَ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ عِلْمًا (٩٨) كَذَلِكَ نَقُصُّ عَلَيْكَ مِنْ أَنْبَاءِ مَا قَدْ سَبَقَ وَقَدْ آتَيْنَاكَ مِنْ لَدُنَّا ذِكْرًا (٩٩)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَسِعَ): it is read with kasra on the sīn and light.
And عِلْمًا is a tamyīz (specification), i.e. "His knowledge encompasses everything".
It is also read with the shadda and fatḥa [وَسَّعَ], and it is then transitive to two objects; the meaning is "He gave everything knowledge".
There is another view on it: that it is in the sense of "He made great the creation of every great thing, such as the earth and the sky", and it is in the sense of "He spread out"; so عِلْمًا is a tamyīz.
(كَذَلِكَ): an adjective of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "a narrating like that", i.e. "We narrate a report from among the reports".

ukberi-tibyan:101-101.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (خَالِدِينَ فِيهِ وَسَاءَ لَهُمْ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ حِمْلًا (١٠١)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (خَالِدِينَ): a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in «يَحْمِلُ» (ayah 100). The first pronoun follows the wording of «مَنْ», so it is singular, while «خَالِدِينَ» follows the meaning, so it is plural.
And (حِمْلًا): a tamyīz (specification) of the noun of «سَاءَ»; «سَاءَ» is like بِئْسَ ("how bad"), and the implied form is: "and evil is the load as a load". The implied form ought not to be "and evil is the burden (الوزر)", because the specified noun ought to be from the same wording as the noun of بئس.

ukberi-tibyan:102-103.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (يَوْمَ يُنْفَخُ فِي الصُّورِ وَنَحْشُرُ الْمُجْرِمِينَ يَوْمَئِذٍ زُرْقًا (١٠٢) يَتَخَافَتُونَ بَيْنَهُمْ إِنْ لَبِثْتُمْ إِلَّا عَشْرًا (١٠٣)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (يُنْفَخُ): with yāʾ in the passive (with the agent unnamed), and with nūn and with yāʾ with the agent named [نَنْفُخُ / يَنْفُخُ].
And (زُرْقًا): a ḥāl (circumstantial). And (يَتَخَافَتُونَ): another ḥāl, a badal (substitute) from the first, or a ḥāl from the pronoun in زُرْقًا.

ukberi-tibyan:106-108.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (فَيَذَرُهَا قَاعًا صَفْصَفًا (١٠٦) لَا تَرَى فِيهَا عِوَجًا وَلَا أَمْتًا (٠٧) يَوْمَئِذٍ يَتَّبِعُونَ الدَّاعِيَ لَا عِوَجَ لَهُ وَخَشَعَتِ الْأَصْوَاتُ لِلرَّحْمَنِ فَلَا تَسْمَعُ إِلَّا هَمْسًا (١٠٨)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فَيَذَرُهَا): the pronoun refers to the earth; it has not been mentioned, but the mountains indicate it.
And (قَاعًا): a ḥāl (circumstantial).
And (لَا تَرَى): resumptive (mustaʾnaf); it may also be a ḥāl, or an adjective of the ḥāl.
(لَا عِوَجَ لَهُ): it may be a ḥāl from الداعي, or be resumptive.

ukberi-tibyan:109-109.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (يَوْمَئِذٍ لَا تَنْفَعُ الشَّفَاعَةُ إِلَّا مَنْ أَذِنَ لَهُ الرَّحْمَنُ وَرَضِيَ لَهُ قَوْلًا (١٠٩)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (إِلَّا مَنْ أَذِنَ): «مَنْ» is in the position of the accusative by «تَنْفَعُ».
It is also said: in the position of the nominative, i.e. "except the intercession of the one whom [the Most Merciful] permits"; so it is a badal (substitute).

ukberi-tibyan:111-111.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَعَنَتِ الْوُجُوهُ لِلْحَيِّ الْقَيُّومِ وَقَدْ خَابَ مَنْ حَمَلَ ظُلْمًا (١١١)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَقَدْ خَابَ): it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial), and it may be resumptive (mustaʾnaf).

ukberi-tibyan:112-112.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَمَنْ يَعْمَلْ مِنَ الصَّالِحَاتِ وَهُوَ مُؤْمِنٌ فَلَا يَخَافُ ظُلْمًا وَلَا هَضْمًا (١١٢))
His saying, Exalted is He: (فَلَا يَخَافُ): it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). Whoever reads it in the nominative makes it resumptive, and whoever reads it in the jussive [فَلَا يَخَفْ] takes it as a prohibition.

ukberi-tibyan:113-113.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَكَذَلِكَ أَنْزَلْنَاهُ قُرْآنًا عَرَبِيًّا وَصَرَّفْنَا فِيهِ مِنَ الْوَعِيدِ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَتَّقُونَ أَوْ يُحْدِثُ لَهُمْ ذِكْرًا (١١٣)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَكَذَلِكَ): the kāf is a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "a sending down like that".
(وَصَرَّفْنَا فِيهِ مِنَ الْوَعِيدِ): i.e. "threats", and it is [for] the genus; on the view of al-Akhfash, «مِنْ» is redundant (zāʾida).

ukberi-tibyan:114-114.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (فَتَعَالَى اللَّهُ الْمَلِكُ الْحَقُّ وَلَا تَعْجَلْ بِالْقُرْآنِ مِنْ قَبْلِ أَنْ يُقْضَى إِلَيْكَ وَحْيُهُ وَقُلْ رَبِّ زِدْنِي عِلْمًا (١١٤)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (يُقْضَى): in the passive (with the agent unnamed), and «وَحْيُهُ» is nominative by it. And [it is also read] with nūn and fatḥa on the yāʾ [نَقْضِيَ], with وَحْيَهُ accusative.

ukberi-tibyan:115-115.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَلَقَدْ عَهِدْنَا إِلَى آَدَمَ مِن قَبْلُ فَنَسِيَ وَلَمْ نَجِدْ لَهُ عَزْمَا ١١٥).
His saying, Exalted is He: (لَهُ عَزْمًا): it may be the object of «نَجِدْ» in the sense of "We know". Or عَزْمًا may be the object of «نَجِدْ» in the sense of "We find (نُصِبْ)".
And «لَهُ»: either a ḥāl (circumstantial) from عزم, or attached to نجد.
«[Translator's note: in the first view both words are evidently meant as the two objects of نجد in the sense of "know" (عَزْمًا first, لَهُ second); the text is compressed.]»

ukberi-tibyan:116-116.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَإِذْ قُلْنَا لِلْمَلَائِكَةِ اسْجُدُوا لِآدَمَ فَسَجَدُوا إِلَّا إِبْلِيسَ أَبَى (١١٦)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَبَى): this has been mentioned in [Sūrat] al-Baqara.

ukberi-tibyan:117-117.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (فَقُلْنَا يَا آدَمُ إِنَّ هَذَا عَدُوٌّ لَكَ وَلِزَوْجِكَ فَلَا يُخْرِجَنَّكُمَا مِنَ الْجَنَّةِ فَتَشْقَى (١١٧)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فَتَشْقَى): He used the singular after the dual so that the ends of the ayahs agree, while the meaning is also sound, because Adam, upon him be peace, is the one who earns [the livelihood], and he wept more over the sin than she did.

ukberi-tibyan:119-119.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَأَنَّكَ لَا تَظْمَأُ فِيهَا وَلَا تَضْحَى (١١٩)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَأَنَّكَ): it is read with fatḥa on the hamza, conjoined to the position of «أَلَّا تَجُوعَ» (ayah 118). It is permissible for the opened «أَنَّ» to be governed by إنّ because there is separation between them; the implied form is: "that you have satiety, quenching of thirst and shelter".
It is also read with kasra, as resumptive (istiʾnāf), or conjoined to the first «إِنَّ».
«[Translator's note: the text has «وَالَكِنَّ», evidently for «وَالْكِنَّ» ("shelter").]»

ukberi-tibyan:120-120.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (فَوَسْوَسَ إِلَيْهِ الشَّيْطَانُ قَالَ يَا آدَمُ هَلْ أَدُلُّكَ عَلَى شَجَرَةِ الْخُلْدِ وَمُلْكٍ لَا يَبْلَى (١٢٠)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فَوَسْوَسَ إِلَيْهِ): «وَسْوَسَ» is made transitive with إلى because it is in the sense of "he confided secretly"; and in another place He made it transitive with the lām, because it is in the sense of "he mentioned to him", or it is in the sense of "for his sake".

ukberi-tibyan:121-121.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (فَأَكَلَا مِنْهَا فَبَدَتْ لَهُمَا سَوْآتُهُمَا وَطَفِقَا يَخْصِفَانِ عَلَيْهِمَا مِنْ وَرَقِ الْجَنَّةِ وَعَصَى آدَمُ رَبَّهُ فَغَوَى (١٢١)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فَغَوَى): the majority read it with alif, and it is in the sense of "he went wrong" and "perished".
It was read anomalously with yāʾ and kasra on the wāw [فَغَوِيَ], from غَوِيَ الْفَصِيلُ, when the young camel becomes sick from surfeit of milk; and this [reading] is of no account.

ukberi-tibyan:124-124.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَمَنْ أَعْرَضَ عَنْ ذِكْرِي فَإِنَّ لَهُ مَعِيشَةً ضَنْكًا وَنَحْشُرُهُ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ أَعْمَى (١٢٤))
His saying, Exalted is He: (ضَنْكًا): the majority read it with tanwīn, the alif in pause being a replacement for it. الضَّنْك means narrowness.
It is also read: ضَنْكَى, on the pattern of سَكْرَى.
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَنَحْشُرُهُ): it is read with ḍamma on the rāʾ, as resumptive (istiʾnāf), and with sukūn on it, either because of the succession of vowels, or because it is jussive, construed on the position of the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), which is His saying: «فَإِنَّ لَهُ».
And (أَعْمَى): a ḥāl (circumstantial).

ukberi-tibyan:126-126.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قَالَ كَذَلِكَ أَتَتْكَ آيَاتُنَا فَنَسِيتَهَا وَكَذَلِكَ الْيَوْمَ تُنْسَى (١٢٦)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (كَذَلِكَ): in the position of the accusative, i.e. "We gathered [you] like that", or "We did like that", and "a coming like that", or "a recompense like your turning away", or "a forgetting".

ukberi-tibyan:128-128.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (أَفَلَمْ يَهْدِ لَهُمْ كَمْ أَهْلَكْنَا قَبْلَهُمْ مِنَ الْقُرُونِ يَمْشُونَ فِي مَسَاكِنِهِمْ إِنَّ فِي ذَلِكَ لَآيَاتٍ لِأُولِي النُّهَى (١٢٨)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (يَهْدِ لَهُمْ): concerning its fāʿil (agent) there are two views. One of them: a pronoun referring to the name of Allah the Exalted, i.e. "has Allah not made clear to them"; and «بَيَّنَ» is suspended (muʿallaq, i.e. its governing effect is blocked) here, since it is in the sense of "made known", just as He suspended it in His saying, Exalted is He: (وَتَبَيَّنَ لَكُمْ كَيْفَ فَعَلْنَا بِهِمْ). The second: that the agent is what أهلكنا indicates, i.e. "Our destroying", and the clause explains it.
It is also read with nūn [نَهْدِ].
And (كَمْ): in the position of the accusative by «أَهْلَكْنَا», i.e. "how many a generation We destroyed"; we have dealt with this fully at: (سَلْ بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ).
(يَمْشُونَ): a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the genitive pronoun in «لَهُمْ», i.e. "has it not become clear to the idolaters while they walk in the dwellings of those of the unbelievers whom He destroyed".
It is also said: it is a ḥāl from the object in أهلكنا, i.e. "We destroyed them in the state of their heedlessness".

ukberi-tibyan:129-129.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَلَوْلَا كَلِمَةٌ سَبَقَتْ مِنْ رَبِّكَ لَكَانَ لِزَامًا وَأَجَلٌ مُسَمًّى (١٢٩)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَأَجَلٌ مُسَمًّى): it is conjoined to «كَلِمَةٌ», i.e. "and were it not for an appointed term, the punishment would have been inevitable". اللِّزَام is a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of the active participle. It may also be the plural of لَازِم, like قَائِم and قِيَام.

ukberi-tibyan:130-130.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (فَاصْبِرْ عَلَى مَا يَقُولُونَ وَسَبِّحْ بِحَمْدِ رَبِّكَ قَبْلَ طُلُوعِ الشَّمْسِ وَقَبْلَ غُرُوبِهَا وَمِنْ آنَاءِ اللَّيْلِ فَسَبِّحْ وَأَطْرَافَ النَّهَارِ لَعَلَّكَ تَرْضَى (١٣٠)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَمِنْ آنَاءِ اللَّيْلِ): it is in the position of the accusative by the second سَبِّحْ.
(وَأَطْرَافَ): construed on the position [of «وَمِنْ آنَاءِ اللَّيْلِ»], or conjoined to «قَبْلَ».
He put the plural in place of the dual because the day has two ends, and [the dual] has come in His saying: (وَأَقِمِ الصَّلَاةَ طَرَفَيِ النَّهَارِ).
It is also said: since "the day" is a genus, He made the ends plural.
It is also said: by the ends He meant the hours, as He the Exalted said: (وَمِنْ آنَاءِ اللَّيْلِ).
(لَعَلَّكَ تَرْضَى): and (تُرْضَى) [i.e. read in the active and in the passive]; both are clear.
«[Translator's note: the source prints both forms identically as «تَرْضَى»; the variant meant is evidently the passive تُرْضَى.]»

ukberi-tibyan:131-131.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَلَا تَمُدَّنَّ عَيْنَيْكَ إِلَى مَا مَتَّعْنَا بِهِ أَزْوَاجًا مِنْهُمْ زَهْرَةَ الْحَيَاةِ الدُّنْيَا لِنَفْتِنَهُمْ فِيهِ وَرِزْقُ رَبِّكَ خَيْرٌ وَأَبْقَى (١٣١)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (زَهْرَةَ): concerning its accusative there are several views. The first: that it is accusative by an omitted verb indicated by «مَتَّعْنَا», i.e. "We made for them the flower…". The second: that it is a badal (substitute) from the position of «بِهِ».
The third: that it is a badal from أزواج, the implied form being "possessors of the flower", the muḍāf having been omitted.
It may also be that He made the pairs [themselves] a flower, by way of hyperbole. It cannot be an adjective, because it is
definite while أزواجًا is indefinite. The fourth: that it is [accusative] for censure, i.e. "I censure" or "I mean". The fifth: that it is a badal from «مَا»; some chose this. Others said it is not permissible, because His saying, Exalted is He: (لِنَفْتِنَهُمْ) belongs to the ṣila (relative clause) of متّعنا, so it would entail separating the ṣila from the relative noun by something extraneous.
The sixth: that it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the hāʾ, or from «مَا», with the tanwīn dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, and الحياة put in the genitive as a badal from «مَا». Makkī chose this, and it is questionable.
The seventh: that it is a tamyīz (specification) for «مَا» or for the hāʾ in به; this is reported from al-Farrāʾ, and it is an error, because it is definite.

ukberi-tibyan:132-132.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَأْمُرْ أَهْلَكَ بِالصَّلَاةِ وَاصْطَبِرْ عَلَيْهَا لَا نَسْأَلُكَ رِزْقًا نَحْنُ نَرْزُقُكَ وَالْعَاقِبَةُ لِلتَّقْوَى (١٣٢))
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَالْعَاقِبَةُ لِلتَّقْوَى): i.e. "for the possessors of taqwā (God-consciousness)"; this is indicated by His saying: (وَالْعَاقِبَةُ لِلتَّقْوَى).
«[Translator's note: the proof-text is printed exactly like the phrase being explained; another verse, such as ﴿وَالْعَاقِبَةُ لِلْمُتَّقِينَ﴾, may have been intended.]»

ukberi-tibyan:133-134.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَقَالُوا لَوْلَا يَأْتِينَا بِآيَةٍ مِنْ رَبِّهِ أَوَلَمْ تَأْتِهِمْ بَيِّنَةُ مَا فِي الصُّحُفِ الْأُولَى (١٣٣) وَلَوْ أَنَّا أَهْلَكْنَاهُمْ بِعَذَابٍ مِنْ قَبْلِهِ لَقَالُوا رَبَّنَا لَوْلَا أَرْسَلْتَ إِلَيْنَا رَسُولًا فَنَتَّبِعَ آيَاتِكَ مِنْ قَبْلِ أَنْ نَذِلَّ وَنَخْزَى (١٣٤)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَوَلَمْ تَأْتِهِمْ): it is read with tāʾ according to the wording of البيّنة ("the clear proof"), and with yāʾ according to the meaning of البيان ("the explanation").
«بَيِّنَةٌ» has also been read with tanwīn, with «مَا» a badal (substitute) from it, or the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject). It is reported from some that it was read in the accusative with tanwīn [بَيِّنَةً], on the basis that the agent is «مَا» and «بَيِّنَةً» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) placed first.
And (الصُّحُفِ): with a vowel [on the ḥāʾ] and with sukūn [الصُّحْفِ].
(فَنَتَّبِعَ): the answer to the question.
And (نَذِلَّ وَنَخْزَى): with the agent named and with it unnamed [نُذَلَّ وَنُخْزَى].

ukberi-tibyan:135-135.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قُلْ كُلٌّ مُتَرَبِّصٌ فَتَرَبَّصُوا فَسَتَعْلَمُونَ مَنْ أَصْحَابُ الصِّرَاطِ السَّوِيِّ وَمَنِ اهْتَدَى (١٣٥)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مَنْ أَصْحَابُ): «مَنْ» is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and «أَصْحَابُ» a khabar (predicate), and the clause is in the position of the accusative. «مَنْ» cannot be in the sense of الذي, since there is no pronoun returning to it; that [view] has been reported from al-Farrāʾ.
(الصِّرَاطِ السَّوِيِّ): there are five readings of it. The first: on the pattern faʿīl, i.e. "the level one".
The second: السَّوَاء, i.e. "the middle". The third: السَّوْء, with fatḥa on the sīn, in the sense of evil. The fourth: السُّوأَى, which is the feminine of الأسوأ ("the worse"); it is made feminine according to the meaning of الصراط, i.e. الطريقة ("the way"), as in His saying, Exalted is He: (اسْتَقَامُوا عَلَى الطَّرِيقَةِ). The fifth: السُّوَيّ, as the diminutive of السَّوْء.
And (مَنْ أَصْحَابُ): in the sense of الذي; in it there is the conjoining of a statement to a question, and in it there is support for the view of al-Farrāʾ.
«مَنْ» may also be in the position of the genitive, i.e. "and the companions of the one who is guided", meaning the Prophet ﷺ. It may also be interrogative like the first.
«[Translator's note: the heading of the last paragraph is printed «(مَنْ أَصْحَابُ)», but the discussion concerns «وَمَنِ اهْتَدَى».]»

ukberi-tibyan:1-1.t:
(طه): the discussion of it has been given under the view in which it is taken as disconnected letters. It is also said: its meaning is "O man", as a vocative (munādā). It is also said: «طَا» is an imperative verb, originally with hamza [«طَأْ», "tread"], but an alif was substituted for the hamza, and «هَا» is the pronoun of the earth.
And it is read «طَهْ»; concerning the hāʾ there are two views. The first: it is a substitute for the hamza, as it was substituted in «أَرَقْتُ», so that «هَرَقْتُ» was said. The second: he substituted an alif for the hamza, then dropped it because of the indeclinability [of the imperative], and attached to it the hāʾ of pause (hāʾ al-sakt).

ukberi-tibyan:2-3.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (مَا أَنْزَلْنَا عَلَيْكَ الْقُرْآنَ لِتَشْقَى (٢) إِلَّا تَذْكِرَةً لِمَنْ يَخْشَى (٣)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (إِلَّا تَذْكِرَةً): it is a disconnected exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ), i.e. "but We sent it down as a reminder", i.e. for the sake of reminding.
It is also said: it is a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "but We reminded by it with a reminding". It cannot be a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose) of the «أَنْزَلْنَا» mentioned, because that has already taken an object of purpose, namely «لِتَشْقَى», so it does not take another of the same kind; nor is it sound for «لِتَشْقَى» to govern it, because the meaning would be corrupted. It is also said: «تَذْكِرَةً» is a maṣdar in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial).

ukberi-tibyan:4-4.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (تَنْزِيلًا مِمَّنْ خَلَقَ الْأَرْضَ وَالسَّمَاوَاتِ الْعُلَا (٤)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (تَنْزِيلًا): it is a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "We sent it down a sending down". It is also said: it is the object of «يَخْشَى», and «مِنْ» is attached to it.
And (الْعُلَا): the plural of «الْعُلْيَا».

ukberi-tibyan:6-6.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (لَهُ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا وَمَا تَحْتَ الثَّرَى (٦)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (لَهُ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ): a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate); or «مَا» is made nominative by the adverbial phrase.
One of the extremists said: «مَا» is the agent of «اسْتَوَى» [in the previous verse]; this is far-fetched. Moreover, it does not help him in [his] interpretation, since His saying (الرَّحْمَنُ عَلَى الْعَرْشِ) would remain a complete sentence, and that is precisely what he was fleeing from. There are other interpretations of the verse which the iʿrāb does not rule out.

ukberi-tibyan:7-7.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَإِنْ تَجْهَرْ بِالْقَوْلِ فَإِنَّهُ يَعْلَمُ السِّرَّ وَأَخْفَى (٧)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَأَخْفَى): it may be a verb whose object is omitted, i.e. "and He concealed the secret from creation". It may also be a noun [an elative], i.e. "and what is more hidden than it".
